items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It's a very self-contained little clique of composers. It's Goldsmith and Schifrin and Pat . . .

ctx.x: Was it easier writing music for television than it was writing music for films? I notice on the film credits [that] these are primarily films that were aimed toward a black market in the black community, films like Cleopatra Jones. I’m just wondering if it was any easier to get work as far as television writing than it was writing for feature films.

Yes, it was easier. Al Bart had an easier time of getting assignments for me for television than for feature films. If the truth be told, there are only a few feature film composers who do most of the films in Hollywood. It's a very self-contained little clique of composers. It's Goldsmith and Schifrin and Pat . . .
